inspected_anchors.finding: Three-stage literature retrieval, causal-pair extraction and hypothesis generation.
PMC open-access selection, journal-title filter,43,312 articles,35,797 from Frontiers in Psychology; PyPDF2 cleaning.
Prompt explicitly extracts both causality and correlation;4000-token chunks, model filtering and expert feedback;197k concepts/235k links;156/238 causal agreement,31/238 nonexistent.
node2vec similarity shortlist and neighbor Jaccard ranking; graph predictions generate testable hypotheses rather than tested mechanisms.
130 hypotheses; random30 and expert-selected30;13 responding doctoral students produced41, sampled30; different selection processes.
Claude2 generates50 and GPT4 selects30; three expert raters, randomized order; reviewer agreement varies; BERT/tSNE are semantic diagnostics.
Rater-standardized averaged novelty scores; reported novelty advantage; no equivalence design.
Table5 expert-selected mean comparison p=.085, median p=.550; usefulness F(3,116)=5.25 paired with p=.553; GPT4 ablation60 versus60.
Ablation novelty advantage and usefulness p=.1937; semantic F(3,1652)=84.1611 with claimed R2=.8696; pair-distance dependence needs raw design.
Sparse graph, synonymous concepts, extraction errors and restricted130-hypothesis evaluation acknowledged.
Authors identify shift of expert work from generation to evaluation; data partly supplementary, additional data on request.
Supplement pointer, author roles and CC-BY4 article license; it does not license every corpus/code dependency.

supported_claims: The paper combines GPT4 literature relation extraction, Neo4j graph storage, node2vec/Jaccard link ranking and generated psychological hypotheses.
It reports43,312 articles,197k concepts and235k links; corpus selection and source concentration constrain coverage.
The prompt distinguishes causal/correlational labels;156 of238 predicted causal pairs agree with human causal labels,31 are not recognized as relationships.
The main comparison uses30 hypotheses per arm with different random, expert and model-selection pipelines; three experts rate novelty and utility.
Reported novelty gains and nonsignificant utility contrasts concern these selected ideas and raters; the study does not experimentally validate proposed interventions.
The revised article explicitly retains extraction error, sparse/synonymous concepts, limited evaluated hypotheses and expert-evaluation bottlenecks.
limitations: Bounded author primary-text review; no independent reproduction or complete literature coverage.
Selected July2024 arXiv v3 contains the14-page journal article; current publisher supplement, raw ratings and code were not acquired or qualified.
Earlier58-page v1 is preserved separately; its appendix is not silently substituted for the revised supplement.
Model snapshots, code dependencies, graph conventions and full corpus rights remain unqualified.
Reported novelty/utility ratings do not establish causal truth, calibrated effects or bank transfer.
No live model, downloaded code or upstream experiments executed; no rendered acceptance.

F84.1611 at3,1652 implies ordinary R2 about.132573, not.8696.
Identical undirected neighborhoods give Jaccard1 while a structural intervention effect is0; assumed margin80 is invalid versus true-20.
limitations: Project arithmetic and constructed structural law; no reproduction of paper raw data.
ANOVA identities are conditional on the ordinary stated model and printed degrees of freedom.
Jaccard witness does not assert the uninspected native implementation uses this neighbor convention.
No causal calibration, native execution, live model or measured bank return.
